1.c4 Nf6 2.g3 g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 4.d4 O-O 5.Nc.strategy: Completes the kingside development and adds a second guard of e5 and d4, so White can castle next. The position is sound and flexible, and space together with the long diagonal bishop decide the long fight.
Piles on d4 with a developing move and invites d5, after which the knight can jump to a5 to attack the c4 pawn, the soft spot of this set-up. A combative choice, much sharper than the quiet systems.
1.c4 Nf6 2.g3 g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 4.d4 O-O 5.Nc.name: King's Indian Defence: Fianchetto Variation, Carlsbad Variation

1.c4 Nf6 2.g3 g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 4.d4 O-O 5.Nc.strategy: Puts the knight on the square that backs a later advance of the e-pawn and leaves the c-pawn free. A flexible, slower set-up that challenges White's centre from behind.
1.c4 Nf6 2.g3 g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 4.d4 O-O 5.Nc.name: King's Indian Defence: Fianchetto Variation, Debrecen Defence

1.c4 Nf6 2.g3 g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 4.d4 O-O 5.Nc.strategy: Attacks d4 with a pawn at once, so White must choose between closing the centre and releasing the tension. Black loosens the queenside but gets quick counterplay against the white centre.
1.c4 Nf6 2.g3 g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 4.d4 O-O 5.Nc.name: King's Indian Defence: Fianchetto Variation, Yugoslav Variation, Rare Line

1.c4 Nf6 2.g3 g6 3.Bg2 Bg7 4.d4 O-O 5.Nc.strategy: A quiet, solid move that frees the c7 square for the queen but does not touch White's centre directly. White can complete development undisturbed and pick the plan.
